description: I happened across this quote from prof.dr.Edsger W.Dijkstra, circa 1968: "In the mid-sixties we observed what was then known as "the software failure" or "the software crisis". Its emergence was no surprise, its occurrence had been predicted. In not much more than ten years the power of commonly available computers had increased by a factor of thousand, and our programming ability had not increased in proportion. Besides that, the logically simple, sequential machines of the fifties had been replaced by much more complicated pieces of equipment, complicated by such features as multi-level stores and asynchronously active peripherals. It was very clear that the programming task was outgrowing our programming capacities and the emergence of the software crisis was, as said, no surprise....
